name: The Minsky Moment
statement: Long periods of financial stability encourage rising leverage and risk-taking that eventually produce a sudden, self-reinforcing collapse in asset values.
statementAccent: Long periods of financial stability encourage rising leverage
meaning: Hyman Minsky’s financial instability hypothesis argues that capitalist economies are inherently prone to cycles of stability breeding instability: calm periods lower perceived risk, prompting borrowers and lenders to take on progressively riskier debt until the system becomes fragile. A "Minsky moment" is the point at which that fragility snaps into a sudden collapse of asset prices and credit.
mechanism: Minsky classified borrowers into hedge finance (cash flow covers principal and interest), speculative finance (covers only interest, needing refinancing), and Ponzi finance (covers neither, relying on rising asset prices). During prosperity the mix shifts from hedge toward speculative and Ponzi finance; when asset prices stop rising, those borrowers cannot refinance, forcing distressed sales that drive prices down further and can push even sound borrowers into distress.

examples.text: PIMCO economist Paul McCulley coined the term "Minsky moment" in 1998 to describe the sudden collapse triggered by the Russian debt crisis, naming it after Hyman Minsky.
The 2007–2008 subprime and credit crisis is widely cited as the most prominent modern "Minsky moment," with McCulley identifying August 2007 as the pivotal turning point.
Some analysts instead point to the June 2007 collapse of two Bear Stearns-managed subprime hedge funds as an earlier marker of the same episode.

whyItMatters: Largely ignored by mainstream economics during Minsky’s lifetime, the framework gained wide acceptance after 2008 as a leading explanation for debt-driven boom-and-bust cycles, and it now informs macroprudential financial-regulation debates.
limits: The hypothesis is a qualitative, narrative account of credit cycles rather than a formalised predictive model, making it hard to test rigorously or to pinpoint in advance when a "moment" will occur; economists have long been divided on how central instability is to normal market functioning.
misreadings: A "Minsky moment" is often used in media as a synonym for any market crash, but in Minsky’s framework it specifically refers to the collapse following a debt-financed boom driven by the hedge-to-speculative-to-Ponzi shift, not any sudden price drop.
origin: Hyman Minsky (1919–1996) developed the financial instability hypothesis from the early 1970s through his 1986 book "Stabilizing an Unstable Economy"; the term "Minsky moment" was coined by Paul McCulley in 1998.

sources.text: Minsky moment, Wikipedia. — the 1998 McCulley coinage after the Russian crisis and the 2008 crisis as its prominent modern example.
Hyman Minsky, Wikipedia. — his dates and the financial instability hypothesis, including the shift between robustness and fragility.
